about: Source of truth for trlibrary.com delights. Edit here, then run: node scripts/build.mjs. Rules: {"date":"MM-DD"}, {"nth":[month, weekday 0=Sun, n or -1 for last]}, {"election":true}, {"dates":["YYYY-MM-DD"]}, {"live":"aurora|snow"}, {"keyword":"word"}. span = number of days it runs (default 1). Higher priority wins when two land on the same day; a quiet entry blocks everything below it. review: "ok" once facts and links are checked, otherwise what still needs checking. Entries with enabled:false never play on the live site but can be previewed.

eggs.title: T.R.'s birthday
eggs.headline: Happy Birthday, T.R.!
eggs.text: Theodore Roosevelt was born in New York City on October 27, 1858.

eggs.title: Kettle Hill and San Juan Heights
eggs.headline: July 1, 1898
eggs.text: Roosevelt led the Rough Riders up Kettle Hill beside regular cavalry, including Black troopers of the 9th, then charged across the valley to the main San Juan ridge, outside Santiago, Cuba.
eggs.notes: HistorianPanel 2026-10-27: copy closed (Rough Riders ch. IV; 9th Cavalry Troop H report). Keep 'Kettle Hill', not 'San Juan Hill'. Charge scene checked 2026-10-27 (sp-period-visuals, sp-navy-rough-riders; T.R., The Rough Riders ch. I and IV; R. H. Davis, Notes of a War Correspondent; Morton, 3rd Cavalry report): T.R. mounted on Little Texas, orderly Bardshar just ahead, dismounting ~40 yards from the top at a wire fence; troopers on foot in slouch hats and shirtsleeves with Krag carbines, no bayonets or sabres; one plain red-over-white troop guidon (G, E and F troops' guidons were first planted); blue polka-dot havelock streaming behind his hat (Davis, single eyewitness); midday sun (advance ~12:15 p.m.); ranch buildings and a huge iron kettle on the crest, 'probably' for sugar. No hat-waving on the climb (he waved it at the foot, giving the order). Card copy revised 2026-10-27 (Pass A + blind Pass B: Rough Riders ch. IV; NARA Prologue; NPS Buffalo Soldiers): names the regulars, keeps the two charges distinct; 'main San Juan ridge' chosen over 'next ridge' because Kettle Hill is itself on the San Juan Heights.

eggs.title: Independence Day and the Dickinson oration
eggs.headline: Happy Independence Day
eggs.text: On July 5, 1886, Roosevelt was the orator of the day at Dickinson's first Fourth of July celebration in Dakota Territory. July 4 fell on a Sunday that year.
eggs.notes: HistorianPanel 2026-10-27 (Pass A + blind Pass B): celebration held Monday, July 5, 1886 (St. Paul Daily Globe, July 6, 1886, p. 4, dispatch dated July 5; Dickinson Press 'last Monday', reprinted in Hagedorn). 'Orator of the day' is the Press's phrase; John A. Rea also spoke. Earlier copy (July 4; 'one of his first major speeches') was wrong. Many later sources say July 4.

eggs.title: Nobel Peace Prize
eggs.headline: December 10, 1906
eggs.text: Roosevelt became the first American awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, for his work to end the Russo-Japanese War.

eggs.title: The teddy bear hunt
eggs.headline: The teddy bear turns another year older
eggs.text: On a November 1902 hunt in Mississippi, Roosevelt refused to shoot a bear that had been tied up for him. A newspaper cartoon of the moment inspired the teddy bear.
eggs.notes: Period visuals checked 2026-10-27: oak, ash and cypress bottomland 'choked' with undergrowth and canebrake, with a slough (1902 Smedes, Miss. wire report). No bear, hunters or people shown. Leaf colors are plausible but undocumented, so kept muted.

eggs.title: T.R. arrives in the Badlands
eggs.headline: Welcome to the Badlands
eggs.text: In September 1883, a young New Yorker stepped off the train at Little Missouri, Dakota Territory, to hunt bison.
eggs.notes: HistorianPanel 2026-10-27: station (Little Missouri, Dakota Territory) and purpose (to hunt bison) closed. Exact day unresolved: Hagedorn and the TR Center put the 2-3 a.m. arrival on Sept 7, Morris and the NPS handbook on Sept 8; T.R.'s first letter home is datelined 'Little Missouri, Da. Sept 8th 1883'. Runs Sept 7-8 and the copy names only the month. Curator question: read the body of the Sept 8 letter (Houghton MS Am 1541.9 (64-111); TR Center o283352) for when the train set him down.

eggs.title: North Dakota statehood
eggs.headline: Happy Statehood Day, North Dakota
eggs.text: North Dakota joined the Union on November 2, 1889.

eggs.title: Pelican Island
eggs.headline: March 14, 1903
eggs.text: Roosevelt set aside Florida's Pelican Island as the first federal bird reservation, the start of today's National Wildlife Refuge System.

eggs.title: The Antiquities Act
eggs.headline: June 8, 1906
eggs.text: Roosevelt signed the Antiquities Act, the law he used to protect places like Devils Tower and the Grand Canyon.

eggs.title: Devils Tower
eggs.headline: September 24, 1906
eggs.text: Roosevelt proclaimed Wyoming's Devils Tower the first national monument.

eggs.title: Grand Canyon National Monument
eggs.headline: January 11, 1908
eggs.text: Roosevelt protected the Grand Canyon as a national monument. It became a national park in 1919.

eggs.title: The Forest Service
eggs.headline: February 1, 1905
eggs.text: Roosevelt signed the Transfer Act, putting the nation's forest reserves under the agency that became the U.S. Forest Service.

eggs.title: Earth Day
eggs.headline: Happy Earth Day
eggs.text: The land Roosevelt protected is still yours to explore. Get outside today.

eggs.title: Arbor Day
eggs.headline: Happy Arbor Day
eggs.text: In 1907, Roosevelt wrote an Arbor Day message to the nation's schoolchildren about why trees matter. Plant one today.
eggs.notes: HistorianPanel 2026-10-27: letter 'To the School Children of the United States', April 15, 1907 (Forest History Society transcription; CRS R48749). Any quoted line needs a separate quote check.

eggs.title: National Park Service birthday
eggs.headline: Happy Birthday, National Park Service
eggs.text: Congress created the National Park Service on August 25, 1916, to care for parks like the ones Roosevelt helped protect.

eggs.title: Theodore Roosevelt National Memorial Park
eggs.headline: April 25, 1947
eggs.text: Congress set aside Theodore Roosevelt National Memorial Park in the Badlands, including the site of his Elkhorn Ranch.
eggs.notes: HistorianPanel 2026-10-27: 61 Stat. 52, approved April 25, 1947. The 1947 park covered roughly today's South Unit plus the Elkhorn site; the North Unit came in 1948.

eggs.title: Theodore Roosevelt National Park
eggs.headline: November 10, 1978
eggs.text: Theodore Roosevelt National Memorial Park became Theodore Roosevelt National Park.
eggs.notes: HistorianPanel 2026-10-27: Pub. L. 95-625 sec. 610, approved November 10, 1978 (renaming only).

eggs.title: National Public Lands Day
eggs.headline: Happy National Public Lands Day
eggs.text: Find the places Roosevelt protected, and go exploring.

eggs.title: National Hunting and Fishing Day

photo.credit: Photo: Acroterion, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

eggs.headline: Happy National Hunting and Fishing Day
eggs.text: Hunters and anglers were some of Roosevelt's strongest allies in conservation.
eggs.review: Shares a date with National Public Lands Day, which wins. Lower its priority or change the rule if you want it to play.

eggs.title: National Wildlife Refuge Week
eggs.headline: It's National Wildlife Refuge Week
eggs.text: The refuge system began with Pelican Island in 1903 and now protects wildlife in every state.
eggs.notes: HistorianPanel 2026-10-27: FWS states at least one refuge in every state; Pelican Island, March 14, 1903.

eggs.title: World Migratory Bird Day
eggs.headline: Happy World Migratory Bird Day
eggs.text: Roosevelt was a lifelong birder. As President, he established more than 50 federal bird reservations.
eggs.notes: HistorianPanel 2026-10-27: 51 bird reservations, Mar 14, 1903 to Mar 2, 1909 (Biological Survey Circular 87, 1912; matches the Autobiography). Do not use the figure 55, which includes 4 game preserves.

eggs.title: World Wildlife Day

photo.credit: Photo: Acroterion, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

eggs.headline: Happy World Wildlife Day
eggs.text: Pronghorn, bison and wild horses still roam the Badlands Roosevelt knew.

eggs.title: Bison named the national mammal

photo.credit: Photo: Michael Holley, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

eggs.headline: May 9, 2016
eggs.text: The bison became the national mammal of the United States. Bison first brought Roosevelt to the Badlands in 1883.

eggs.title: National Bison Day

photo.credit: Photo: Michael Holley, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

eggs.headline: Happy National Bison Day
eggs.text: Bison first brought Roosevelt to the Badlands in 1883. You can still see them in Theodore Roosevelt National Park.

eggs.title: World Rivers Day

photo.credit: Photo: Acroterion, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

eggs.headline: Happy World Rivers Day
eggs.text: Roosevelt's Elkhorn Ranch sat on the banks of the Little Missouri River.

eggs.title: National Trails Day
eggs.headline: Happy National Trails Day
eggs.text: Roosevelt preached the strenuous life. Find a Badlands trail and take a hike.

eggs.title: World Ranger Day
eggs.headline: Happy World Ranger Day
eggs.text: Thank you to the rangers who care for Theodore Roosevelt National Park and public lands everywhere.

eggs.title: The Panama Canal opens
eggs.headline: August 15, 1914
eggs.text: The Panama Canal opened to ships. Roosevelt had made building it a goal of his presidency.

eggs.title: National Teddy Bear Day
eggs.headline: Happy National Teddy Bear Day
eggs.text: The teddy bear is named for Theodore Roosevelt, after a 1902 hunting trip in Mississippi.

eggs.title: Read Across America Day
eggs.headline: Happy Read Across America Day
eggs.text: Roosevelt was a lifelong reader and the author of dozens of books. What are you reading?
eggs.notes: HistorianPanel 2026-10-27: 'dozens' holds under every count (about 35 to 45 depending on what counts as a book). Never state an exact number without defining it.

eggs.title: International Museum Day
eggs.headline: Happy International Museum Day
eggs.text: Come see Roosevelt's story in the Badlands where it took shape.

eggs.title: National Voter Registration Day
eggs.headline: Step into the arena
eggs.text: It's National Voter Registration Day. Make sure you're registered.

eggs.title: Constitution Day

eggs.headline: Happy Constitution Day
eggs.text: The Constitution was signed on September 17, 1787.
eggs.notes: HistorianPanel 2026-10-27: signed Sept. 17, 1787 (dating clause). Script image from NARA NAID 1667751 (engrossed parchment, RG 11) via Wikimedia/DPLA, public domain.

eggs.title: Election Day
eggs.headline: Step into the arena
eggs.text: It's Election Day. Make your voice heard.

eggs.notes: 2026-10-27: even years only (federal general elections), at Matt's direction.

eggs.title: Presidents' Day
eggs.headline: Happy Presidents' Day
eggs.text: Theodore Roosevelt was the 26th President of the United States.

eggs.title: Thanksgiving
eggs.headline: Happy Thanksgiving
eggs.text: From the Badlands, thank you for being part of the Library's story.

eggs.title: Christmas
eggs.headline: Merry Christmas from the Badlands
eggs.text: Wishing you a warm holiday season.

eggs.title: Veterans Day
eggs.headline: Thank you to all who served
eggs.text: On Veterans Day, the Library honors America's veterans.
eggs.notes: HistorianPanel 2026-10-27: full staff under 4 U.S.C. 6(d), 7(m); hoisted briskly (6(b)). Half-staff only by a separate order in a given year.

eggs.title: Deaths of Martha and Alice Roosevelt
eggs.notes: Roosevelt's mother and his wife Alice died on February 14, 1884. Blocks any Valentine's Day delight.

eggs.title: Death of Theodore Roosevelt
eggs.notes: Roosevelt died at Sagamore Hill on January 6, 1919. No animation.

eggs.title: McKinley's death and T.R.'s oath
eggs.notes: Roosevelt took the oath of office on September 14, 1901, the day McKinley died. Not a celebration.

eggs.title: Milwaukee shooting
eggs.notes: Roosevelt was shot in Milwaukee on October 14, 1912. Keep to text on social, nothing animated on the site.

eggs.headline: Northern lights possible tonight
eggs.text: The space weather forecast is strong enough for the aurora to show over Medora after dark.

eggs.title: Snow in Medora
eggs.headline: It's snowing in Medora
eggs.text: The Badlands in snow are worth the trip. Check today's conditions before you go.

eggs.text: You found a secret. It was Roosevelt's word for something excellent.
